known_against.what: Cluster randomised trial, Song and Baicker, JAMA 2019, 321(15): 1491-1501: a wellness programme at 160 worksites of a large US warehouse retail company (32,974 employees) improved two self-reported behaviours but had no significant effect on clinical health, health care spending or use, absenteeism, job tenure or job performance after 18 months.

evidence.quote: there were no significant differences in clinical measures of health, health care spending and utilization, and employment outcomes after 18 months

known_against.what: Randomised trial, Jones, Molitor and Reif, Quarterly Journal of Economics 2019, 134(4): 1747-1791 (NBER working paper 24229), the Illinois Workplace Wellness Study of nearly 5,000 employees: no significant causal effect on medical spending, health behaviours, productivity or self-reported health after more than two years; the confidence intervals rule out 84% of earlier estimates on spending and absenteeism.

evidence.quote: we do not find significant causal effects of treatment on total medical expenditures

known_against.what: Randomised clinical trial, Reif, Chan, Jones, Payne and Molitor, JAMA Internal Medicine 2020, 180(7): 952-960, 4,834 employees: no significant effect on biometrics, medical diagnoses or medical use after 12 or 24 months.

evidence.quote: no significant effects of the program on biometrics, medical diagnoses, or medical use were seen after 12 or 24 months

known_against.what: Cluster randomised trial, three-year follow-up, Song and Baicker, Health Affairs 2021, 40(6): 951-960: no significant differences in self-reported health, clinical markers, health care spending or use, absenteeism, tenure or job performance at three years.

evidence.quote: the longer follow-up did not yield detectable improvements in clinical, economic, or employment outcomes

rules.R1: Every cited URL passes check_urls.py: fetched with HTTP 200, not a soft 404, and the page holds the quote. Critical.
rules.R2: Every row of both tables has a label from labels; a sourced row has a URL and a quote.
rules.K1: At least one sourced Case against row cites a known_against URL (matched by URL prefix after the scheme and a leading www. are removed, never by a word pattern) and its citation passes check_urls.py.
rules.L1: Every sourced Quote is max_quote_words words or fewer.
rules.M1: The One-month test section is present and holds at least 20 words.
rules.A1: One rough artefact (a Word file) is saved in the run folder, or the run's notes say why it could not be saved (a fail).

pass: Three fresh-chat runs, each scored with score_rnd.py --key evals/rnd/holdout-v5/answer-key-holdout-v5.json. Malformed output fails (missing section, renamed column, unknown label, no table). Otherwise pass needs T1, T2, R1, R2, K1, L1, M1 and A1. One critical failure fails the round. All three runs must pass.
counter_metric: Words of output (output.md). A run that games K1 by stacking citations grows the answer; the word count must not rise more than 10% against the version's tier-2 baseline.
